<b>Кальций крови</b> держится в узких пр: Blood calcium is held within narrow limits (2.2–2.6 mmol/L): the excitability of nerves and muscles, blood clotting and the contraction of the heart all depend on it. The sensor is the calcium-sensing receptor of the parathyroid glands (4 yellow dots). As soon as calcium dips slightly, parathyroid hormone (PTH) is released: it frees calcium from bone, retains it in the kidneys and makes the kidneys produce calcitriol, which in turn increases calcium absorption in the intestine. Calcitonin from the thyroid gland plays only a minor role in humans.
<b>Мало кальция в пище</b>. Кишечник отд: Low dietary calcium. The intestine supplies less — calcium falls slightly and PTH rises (secondary hyperparathyroidism). Blood calcium stays almost normal, but the bones pay for it: their “account” gradually dwindles (the femur grows paler). This is how osteoporosis develops over years.
<b>Дефицит витамина D</b> (мало солнца,: Vitamin D deficiency (too little sun, dark skin, old age, intestinal disease). Without calcitriol the intestine absorbs only 10–15% of calcium. PTH is high, calcium and phosphate are low, and bones are poorly mineralized: in children this is rickets (bowed legs, a “rachitic rosary” on the ribs), in adults osteomalacia.
<b>Первичный гиперпаратиреоз</b> — чаще: Primary hyperparathyroidism is most often a benign adenoma of one parathyroid gland that secretes PTH regardless of feedback. Calcium is high, phosphate is low. The classic picture: “stones, bones, abdominal groans and psychic moans” — kidney stones, osteoporosis, abdominal pain, weakness and depression. It is often found incidentally on a blood test.
<b>Гипопаратиреоз</b> — чаще после опера: Hypoparathyroidism most often follows thyroid surgery, when the parathyroid glands are accidentally removed or damaged. Without PTH calcium falls and nerve excitability rises: tingling around the mouth and in the fingers, carpal spasm (“obstetrician’s hand”, red sparks) and, in severe cases, laryngospasm. Treatment is intravenous calcium, then calcium tablets and calcitriol.
<b>Молочные продукты</b>, сыр, рыба с ко: Dairy products, cheese, fish with bones, sesame — and PTH returns to normal, the bones stop losing mineral. An adult needs about 1000 mg of calcium a day.
<b>Витамин D</b> (холекальциферол) в кап: Vitamin D (cholecalciferol) as drops or tablets, summer sun — and the intestine absorbs calcium again; PTH falls and bones become mineralized.
<b>Операция</b> — удаление аденомы. Уров: Surgery — removal of the adenoma. PTH falls within minutes, calcium normalizes within days; bones recover over years.
<b>Кальций и кальцитриол</b> (активный в: Calcium and calcitriol (active vitamin D, which the kidneys can hardly make on their own without PTH) keep calcium at the lower limit of normal.
<b>Витамин D</b> — скорее гормон, чем ви: Vitamin D is more a hormone than a vitamin. In the skin, ultraviolet B breaks ring B of 7-dehydrocholesterol, turning it into cholecalciferol (D₃; it also comes from fish, eggs and supplements). The liver adds an OH at position 25, giving calcidiol (25-OH-D), the main circulating form; it is used to judge vitamin D stores (normal — from 30 ng/mL). The kidneys add an OH at position 1 — this is calcitriol, the active hormone. Its synthesis is switched on by PTH and low phosphate and switched off by calcitriol itself and FGF23; any excess is broken down by 24-hydroxylase (gray arrow).
<b>Кость всё время перестраивается</b>:: Bone is constantly remodeled: about 10% of the skeleton is replaced each year. An osteoclast (purple, multinucleated) attaches to bone and secretes acid and cathepsin K, dissolving mineral and collagen; calcium enters the blood (light blue sparks). Then osteoblasts (green) line the pit and lay down collagen (osteoid), on which hydroxyapatite Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂ crystallizes. As long as the two processes are balanced, bone mass stays constant.
<b>Постоянно высокий ПТГ</b>: рецепторы: Persistently high PTH: PTH receptors are found on osteoblasts, not osteoclasts — osteoblasts display RANKL, which activates osteoclasts. Resorption outpaces formation and bone loses mass. The paradox: brief daily “shots” of PTH (teriparatide) instead build bone — this is how severe osteoporosis is treated.
<b>Кальцитонин</b> из C-клеток щитовидно: Calcitonin from the C cells of the thyroid gland inhibits osteoclasts directly — they shrink and stop digging. In humans its role in everyday life is small (calcium does not change after the thyroid gland is removed), but it is a marker of medullary thyroid cancer.
<b>Менопауза</b>: эстрогены сдерживали о: Menopause: estrogens held osteoclasts in check (via osteoprotegerin, a “decoy” for RANKL). Without them resorption increases and formation cannot keep up: up to 20% of bone mass is lost in the first 5–7 years — postmenopausal osteoporosis, with fractures of the femoral neck and vertebrae.
<b>Бисфосфонаты</b> (алендронат, золедро: Bisphosphonates (alendronate, zoledronic acid) resemble pyrophosphate and bind tightly to hydroxyapatite. An osteoclast dissolving such bone takes up the drug and loses its activity. Resorption falls and bone mass rises — the mainstay of osteoporosis treatment. Another option is denosumab, an antibody against RANKL.
<b>Хроническая болезнь почек</b>: 1α-гид: Chronic kidney disease: there is too little 1α-hydroxylase — no calcitriol, although D₃ and 25-OH-D are normal. Calcium is poorly absorbed, phosphate accumulates, PTH rises — renal osteodystrophy. Ordinary vitamin D will not help: the active form is given directly (calcitriol, alfacalcidol).
<b>Мало солнца</b>: зимой на широте Моск: Too little sun: in winter, at the latitude of Moscow there is almost no ultraviolet B, and indoors behind glass there is none at all. The 25-OH-D reserve is used up over weeks, and by spring it falls below normal in many people. The kidneys still maintain calcitriol (PTH rises), but at the expense of the bones.
Килограмм кальция лежит в костях, а в кр: There is a kilogram of calcium in the bones, but less than a gram in the blood. Parathyroid hormone and vitamin D make sure that gram does not shift by even one percent.
\n <div><h2>Обмен кальция и фосфата:
Calcium and phosphate metabolism

The body contains about 1 kg of calcium, 99% of it in bone as hydroxyapatite. Total plasma calcium is 2.2–2.6 mmol/L: almost half is bound to albumin, and the active fraction is ionized calcium (1.1–1.3 mmol/L). Acidosis increases the ionized fraction, alkalosis (for example, with hyperventilation) decreases it — cramps may occur.

Hormones

  • Parathyroid hormone (84 amino acids): bone — resorption via RANKL on osteoblasts; kidneys — Ca²⁺ reabsorption, phosphate excretion, calcitriol synthesis.
  • Calcitriol (1,25-(OH)₂-D₃): nuclear receptor VDR; in the intestine it switches on calcium-absorption proteins (TRPV6, calbindin), acts on bone and kidneys, inhibits PTH.
  • Calcitonin (C cells of the thyroid gland): inhibits osteoclasts.
  • FGF23 from bone promotes phosphate excretion and inhibits calcitriol synthesis.

Diseases

Hyper- and hypoparathyroidism, rickets and osteomalacia, osteoporosis, renal osteodystrophy, hypercalcemia of malignancy (PTH-related peptide).

Simplifications

  • Vitamin D molecules follow their chemical formulas; organs, cells and the bone surface are schematic.
  • Calcium and PTH levels come from a simple feedback model; the numbers are typical, not diagnostic.
  • Bone remodeling is shown thousands of times faster: a real cycle takes 3–6 months.
